claims.text: A simulation-calibrated, low-power re-melting pass after standard LPBF melting will reduce thermal gradients in CoCrFeMnNi.
The re-melting pass will enable partial in situ annealing.
The dual-stage process will refine the CoCrFeMnNi microstructure relative to single-pass LPBF.
The dual-stage process will reduce residual stresses and fabrication-induced defects relative to single-pass LPBF.
The proposed process uses real-time thermal feedback and simulation-calibrated parameters to adapt the re-melting pass.
The re-melting pass is to be applied immediately after deposition of each layer under an inert atmosphere with the substrate preheated to 200–300 °C.
The intervention will produce a homogenized microstructure with uniformly distributed grains.
Re-heating the recently solidified layer will promote slower and more uniform solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients and more uniform solidification will minimize residual-stress accumulation and defect formation.
Controlled thermal management will enhance dimensional stability.
Adaptive dual-stage LPBF will reduce warping and distortion and improve dimensional tolerances relative to standard single-pass LPBF.
Adaptive dual-stage LPBF will increase tensile strength and fatigue resistance relative to standard single-pass LPBF.
Adaptive dual-stage LPBF will lower porosity, micro-cracking, and overall defect incidence relative to standard single-pass LPBF.
Standard single-pass LPBF has higher thermal gradients, residual stresses, and defect counts than the proposed dual-stage process.
Inaccurate sensor feedback or deviations from calibrated re-melting conditions may reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
Overheating during re-melting may cause microstructural coarsening.
